text: The Crypt was an indoor Giant Top Spin ride located at Kings Island in Mason, Ohio. It was designed and manufactured by Paramount Parks in collaboration with HUSS Park Attractions and originally opened as Tomb Raider: The Ride on April 5, 2002, featuring special effects aligned with the theme of the 2001 film Lara Croft: Tomb Raider from Paramount Pictures. During the 2000 season, Kenton's Cove Keelboat Canal, a log flume water ride, concluded its operations, and the area was fenced in with the message, "An exciting new adventure is coming in 2002." Paramount officially announced Tomb Raider: The Ride on July 2, 2001, by placing a 17-foot-tall (5.2 m) Hindu goddess Brahma prop—used in the film and later in the ride's pre-show—before the park's Eiffel Tower and Royal Fountains. The ride cost approximately $20 million to build, making it one of the most expensive rides ever constructed at the park. It was the world's first and only Giant Top Spin, performing two inversions in a 1:10 cycle. In its original form, the ride included four inversions, extended hang time over lava pits, a god with piercing eyes and fire and ice emblems, fog effects, and a synchronized musical score lasting 2:30, composed by Rob Pottorf, with sound effects from The Bakery and voiceovers from Angelina Jolie and other film cast members. The entry plaza featured a special edition Land Rover Defender representing Lara Croft, atmospheric music (sampling the film's score), and a sequence where guests walked on catwalks over artifacts and rubble, passing under a bamboo-supported ceiling, with a large antechamber containing stone monkey warrior statues dividing guests into three rows. As the original score intensified, ancient gears were heard tumbling into place, aligning a light to illuminate the Triangle of Light on a carved door, which then slid open with sound and fog effects, allowing entry into the pre-show room. The pre-show room included the Brahma statue and a large oval projection screen that raised from an altar, playing a video explaining the ride's storyline centered on the Triangle of Light, an ancient artifact capable of controlling time. After the video ended, the left wall rose to reveal a "secret" entrance to a sixty-foot-tall altar chamber of the god Shiva, allowing riders to board in the same rows. The ride lifted riders to the eyes of a Shiva carving, which scanned them with automated lights and displayed fire and ice emblems in two of his six hands. It then flipped through the darkness, stopping with riders looking up at razor-sharp icy stalactites, flipped again to stop with riders looking down at "lava pits"—pools of water cascading from a massive volcano behind the loading platform—and as the music played, the lava would jump up, narrowly avoiding riders. After another flip, the ride circled around the bottom of its arc, looking up at Shiva, with fog and lights filling the room, and fire and ice effects turning off as the god screamed and his fire, ice, and eyes went dark, only to "wake up" again with a final blast of fog nearly touching riders before fading, a device to maintain engagement during the lengthy homing procedure. In June 2006, Cedar Fair Entertainment Company purchased all five Paramount Parks from Viacom. After the 2007 season, all references to Paramount and their licensed film properties were removed from the park's rides. At Kings Island, this led to the renaming of Tomb Raider: The Ride to The Crypt on January 21, 2008. The name change coincided with a theme shift, including the painting over of the Shiva goddess statue in the Heart of the Tomb, removal of water and fog effects, and a reduction in the 77-seat gondola's capacity to 46 by removing the first row of seats—reducing capacity by one third. The ride performed a nine-inversion cycle in 2008 and for a month in 2009, but beginning in 2009, it was reprogrammed to perform only two inversions—half the number from its original Tomb Raider: The Ride version. The Crypt was updated over time: after operating with a techno soundtrack in complete darkness, it switched to howling wind and beating drums; gradually, theatrical lighting returned. The queue line, which had its Tomb Raider: The Ride music removed earlier, played atmospheric music from the Midnight Syndicate until 2011, when both the queue and ride were outfitted with music from the 2010 film Inception. In 2011, new lighting and props were added to the queue, manual doors replaced the original "vault door," the red, amber, and yellow underwater lights illuminating the "lava pit" were turned back on and remained throughout the ride, and blue lights were installed on the goddess statue, flashing as the gondola reversed halfway through the cycle. The Crypt gave its last ride on October 30, 2011, and was removed from the park's website on January 20, 2012, with park officials confirming on Twitter the following month that it had "reached the end of its service life" and would be "replaced by an all-new Halloween Haunt experience." The Crypt was transformed into Madame Fatale's Cavern of Terror, a themed attraction based on a museum of oddities and wax, which was removed after the 2024 Halloween season. In 2025, Kings Island debuted The Conjuring: Beyond Fear, a new maze attraction themed to the The Conjuring Universe media franchise, in the same building. The show elements for Tomb Raider: The Ride were designed by Technifex, with scenic design by Weber Group and lighting by Visual Terrain; the soundtrack was composed by Rob Pottorf of RPMusic, with sound design by The Bakery. The Travel Channel aired a behind-the-scenes special on the mechanics and story of the original ride. The Crypt was a higher-capacity version of the popular smaller Top Spin ride found at many amusement parks. Initially, Tomb Raider: The Ride accommodated 77 riders, and after rebranding as The Crypt, its capacity was reduced to 46 by removing the first row of seats.
